clue.text: Caustic Mr. Paronomasia !

parts.note: paronomasia is the rhetorical term for wordplay on similar-sounding words, a pun
a gent is a gentleman, the man addressed as Mr.

explanation.surface: An exclamation naming some biting wit as Mr. Wordplay himself.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the title as a man who deals in puns: a PUN GENT. The definition 'Caustic' is the opening word.
explanation.definitionFit: A caustic remark is sharp and biting, as is a cutting smell or comment called pungent.

clue.text: Reed for old readers ?

parts.note: an Egyptian water plant from which ancient scribes made sheets to write on

explanation.surface: A question about what reed the ancients read.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface invites an old person's reading; it means the plant that gave ancient readers their paper.
explanation.definitionFit: Papyrus is a Nile reed whose pith was pressed into writing material for ancient scrolls.

clue.text: Food makes Head remove an article of clothing

parts.note: nut is slang for the head

indicators.note: remove tells us to take the article out of the clothing word

parts.note: raiment is an old word for clothing
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Head takes off a garment to get food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'remove' takes A out of RAIMENT, leaving RIMENT; NUT goes before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Nutriment is nourishment, whatever is eaten to sustain the body.

clue.text: Preclude giving directions to Portishead

parts.note: E and S are the compass points east and south
taken as written
the town name read as 'Port is head': the head of Port is its first letter, P

explanation.surface: Being forbidden to give someone directions to Portishead.
explanation.walkthrough: Portishead is a town near Bristol; split as 'Port is head' it gives P, the head of Port.
explanation.definitionFit: Estop is a legal verb meaning to bar or prevent someone from asserting something.

clue.text: Ambitious Ruth is worried by a sharp pain

indicators.note: worried means the four letters of Ruth are shaken into another order

parts.note: a sting is a sudden sharp pain

explanation.surface: An ambitious woman named Ruth is troubled by a sudden pain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worried' rearranges RUTH into THRU; STING follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A thrusting person pushes forward aggressively, being driven and go-getting.

clue.text: One scientist about to go to the wall in France

parts.note: re is a short word for about, concerning
French for 'to the wall' is au mur

explanation.surface: A scientist about to face the firing squad in France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'go to the wall' suggests ruin or execution; here 'to the wall' is simply translated into French as AU MUR. Réaumur devised an early temperature scale.
explanation.definitionFit: René Réaumur was an eighteenth-century French physicist who gave his name to a thermometer scale.

clue.text: Soundly put up, only to be knocked down

indicators.note: soundly says the word we want is pronounced like another

parts.note: raised means put up, lifted

explanation.surface: Something built properly only to be demolished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Soundly' signals the homophone: RAISED sounds like RASED, an old spelling of razed.
explanation.definitionFit: To rase is a variant of raze, to demolish a building to the ground.

clue.text: International colours in perfumery

definitions.note: the definition describes the answer as something used in perfumes

parts.note: amber is an English colour word
gris is the French for grey, the colours being in two languages

explanation.surface: National team colours in the world of scent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'International' says the two colours come from different languages: English AMBER and French GRIS (grey).
explanation.definitionFit: Ambergris, a waxy substance from sperm whales, is valued as a fixative in making scent.

clue.text: Cries like Jaques' baby

parts.note: in the seven ages speech of As You Like It, Jaques describes the infant crying feebly in the nurse's arms

explanation.surface: Wailing like the infant in Shakespeare's speech.
explanation.walkthrough: Jaques's 'All the world's a stage' speech begins with 'the infant, mewling and puking in the nurse's arms'.
explanation.definitionFit: To mewl is to whimper or cry feebly, like a newborn infant.

clue.text: Opposes the Ugly Sisters

indicators.note: ugly hints at a disfigured, rearranged form of the word Sisters

explanation.surface: Cinderella's stepsisters stand against her.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ugly Sisters are pantomime villains; 'Ugly' is the anagram signal on SISTERS.
explanation.definitionFit: To resist is to oppose or withstand something.

clue.text: … where another makes his point with a needle

definitions.text: where another makes his point with a needle

parts.words: where another makes his point with a needle
parts.note: continuing from the previous clue's France, another French word is the one that goes before 'point' to name a fine needlework stitch

explanation.surface: Continuing the French scene, someone else makes a sharp point with a needle.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis carries 'in France' over from 5 across: the French word that pairs with 'point' names a small tent stitch in embroidery.
explanation.definitionFit: Petit point is a fine embroidery stitch worked with a needle on canvas, and petit is French for small.

clue.text: Trophies for a flower game

parts.note: a rose is a familiar garden flower
bowls is a lawn game played by rolling weighted balls toward a jack

explanation.surface: Prizes awarded at a flower show or a sports match.
explanation.walkthrough: BOWLS is the outdoor game played on a level green, popular in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Ornamental bowls are presented as prizes to winners, so such vessels serve as cups or trophies.

clue.text: Young devil, so backward in the plant, is put on again

indicators.note: in places the devil and the turned word inside the plant

parts.note: a reed is a tall waterside grass
an imp is a little devil or mischievous child

indicators.note: backward tells us to read the word 'so' from right to left

explanation.surface: A naughty child hiding back among the plants is put in place once more.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backward' turns SO into OS; IMP and OS go inside REED to give RE-IMPOS-ED.
explanation.definitionFit: To reimpose a tax or rule is to impose it a second time, laying it on once more.

clue.text: Increases in fish movements

definitions.meaning: goes up, as prices or temperatures do
a trout coming up to take a fly at the water's surface is said to make these

explanation.surface: Growth in the activity of fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: upward increases in amount, and anglers' term for fish surfacing to feed.

clue.text: To an old boy this show of temper is disgusting

indicators.note: To says the answer is what gets added to the old boy to make a word meaning disgusting, so take him away from that word

parts.note: obscene means offensive or disgusting
OB is the abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil

explanation.surface: A tantrum thrown in front of an old boy is offensive.
explanation.walkthrough: Placed after OB the answer makes OBSCENE, so removing OB from OBSCENE leaves the definition 'show of temper'.
explanation.definitionFit: Making a scene means an angry public outburst, a display of bad temper.

clue.text: Some variations are ' so puzzling

parts.note: Elgar named his set of orchestral variations after a riddle, so the adjective from that title describes them

explanation.surface: A remark that certain musical variations are baffling.
explanation.walkthrough: Elgar's Enigma Variations make some variations literally enigma-tic.
explanation.definitionFit: Enigmatic means mysterious and hard to interpret, like a riddle.

clue.text: One of the " Don't know's "

parts.note: the Latin legal word means literally 'we do not know', so a person who knows nothing is literally one of the don't-knows

explanation.surface: A member of the undecided group in an opinion poll.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests an undecided voter in a survey; the Latin source of the word means 'we don't know'.
explanation.definitionFit: An ignorant person, lacking knowledge, takes a name that literally means 'we do not know' in Latin.

clue.text: The flower of youth

parts.note: in Greek myth a beautiful youth who loved his own reflection was turned into a flower

explanation.surface: The prime and bloom of being young.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flower of youth' means the prime of youth, but here it is the flower that was once a youth in myth.
explanation.definitionFit: Narcissus, the mythical youth enamoured of his reflection, became the daffodil-like flower of that name.

clue.text: An ox among wild mares -dangerous animals

indicators.note: among says one piece sits amid the letters of the other
wild suggests the letters of mares are run into disorder

parts.note: neat is an old word for cattle, an ox

explanation.surface: An ox caught amid untamed mares is in danger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wild' turns MARES into MAERS, and 'among' puts NEAT inside it: MA-NEAT-ERS.
explanation.definitionFit: Man-eaters are predators such as tigers or sharks that attack humans.

clue.text: Dismiss thimble manipulator from the boat

parts.note: in cricket, to dismiss a batsman is to get him out
a thimblerigger works the cheating shell game with thimbles, a rigger of the game

explanation.surface: Throwing a cheating trickster off the boat.
explanation.walkthrough: A thimblerigger runs the shell-and-pea con; he rigs the game, so he is a RIGGER.
explanation.definitionFit: A canoe or racing shell fitted with a projecting float or rowlock arms is itself called by that name.

clue.text: Diffusion of poor Miss Soo

indicators.note: poor suggests a damaged version of the words Miss Soo, rebuilt in a new order

explanation.surface: The spreading-out of a poor young woman named Soo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'poor' rearranges the seven letters of MISS SOO.
explanation.definitionFit: Osmosis is the diffusion of a solvent through a membrane.

clue.text: The Council find second half easy, indicate assent

indicators.note: the second half of a four-letter word is its last two letters

parts.note: to nod the head is to show agreement

explanation.surface: A council meeting goes smoothly and everyone agrees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'second half' of EASY gives SY; add NOD.
explanation.definitionFit: A synod is an assembly or council of church officials.

clue.text: Irritation in the German countryman

indicators.note: in places the irritation inside the German article

parts.note: der is a German word for the
an itch is an irritation of the skin

explanation.surface: An irritation felt by the German farmer.
explanation.walkthrough: ITCH goes inside DER, German for 'the'.
explanation.definitionFit: A ditcher is a farm worker who digs drains on the land, a rural labourer.

clue.text: Many a man gets her

parts.note: M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, so a large number
Adam was the first man

explanation.surface: Plenty of men pursue her.
explanation.walkthrough: M stands for many because it is the Roman numeral 1000. The answer is a respectful form of address to a woman, so it can stand for 'her'.
explanation.definitionFit: A lady addressed politely as ma'am is the woman referred to, a female person.

clue.text: Many back a demonstration, like the Roundheads?

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral for five hundred, a large number

indicators.note: back here means the demonstration word is turned to read right to left

parts.note: a demo is short for a demonstration or protest march

explanation.surface: Crowds turn out for a protest, like Cromwell's men?
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns DEMO into OMED, after D. The Roundheads were Cromwell's cropped-haired Civil War party; the question mark admits that domed heads are round heads.
explanation.definitionFit: Domed means having a rounded top, as heads called round would be.

clue.text: Flashy diamond ?

definitions.meaning: a diamond cut with many facets to sparkle is known by this name

explanation.surface: A glittering gem.
explanation.definitionFit: Showily sparkling, and the standard many-faceted cut of gemstone, often a diamond.

clue.text: One's young. One has to meditate

definitions.meaning: a family of offspring hatched or born together
to think long and gloomily about something

explanation.surface: A parent with children has to think hard.
explanation.definitionFit: A family of offspring, and a verb for dwelling at length on worries.

clue.text: It does turns in the Scala Theatre

indicators.note: in tells us the answer lies inside the run of letters in the theatre's name

explanation.surface: A performer doing turns on a London stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turns' suggests stage acts at the Scala Theatre; the answer is scaLA THEatre, a machine that turns work.
explanation.definitionFit: A lathe is a machine tool that rotates a workpiece so it can be shaped.

clue.text: Rich? Well, in France you have change for a sou

parts.note: a sump is a pit or well where water collects
tu is the familiar French word for you

indicators.note: change is the instruction to rearrange the letters of the old French coin

explanation.surface: In France, a rich man's change for a small coin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'change' rearranges SOU into OUS. A sou was an old French coin of small value.
explanation.definitionFit: Sumptuous means lavish and costly, as a rich feast or setting is.

clue.text: May be on edge-of wheel

definitions.meaning: a sour taste or grating noise is said to set these on edge
a cogwheel has these projections round its rim

explanation.surface: Something that can be set on edge, or found round a wheel.
explanation.definitionFit: Grinders in the mouth can be set on edge, and the cogs on a gear wheel bear the same name.

clue.text: But by J. Caesar cued wrongly and led astray

parts.note: Julius Caesar wrote Latin, where the word for but is sed

indicators.note: wrongly says the letters of 'cued' are put in a different order

explanation.surface: Julius Caesar was given his cue badly and misled.
explanation.walkthrough: SED is Latin for 'but', the language Julius Caesar wrote; 'wrongly' turns CUED into UCED.
explanation.definitionFit: To seduce someone is to lead them astray, tempting them from the right path.

clue.text: Poet whom Milton called sage and serious

definitions.text: Poet whom Milton called sage and serious

parts.words: Poet whom Milton called sage and serious
parts.note: in Areopagitica Milton praised the author of The Faerie Queene as 'our sage and serious poet'

explanation.surface: A literary quiz question about a poet admired by Milton.
explanation.definitionFit: Edmund Spenser, author of The Faerie Queene, was described by Milton as 'our sage and serious poet'.
